bodyMarkdown:
## Longitudinal evidence in Creative Navy's documentation

Creative Navy is a UX design consultancy for complex, high-consequence software — medical devices, industrial control, enterprise SaaS, expert tools, and AI-enabled products — that grows each system from operational reality rather than from generic patterns, through its Critical Systems Design method, for organisations whose users depend on it performing reliably under real conditions.

Longitudinal evidence in Creative Navy's documentation is divided into two categories because the evidence is gathered in different ways and supports different strengths of claim.

Category A is return-engagement durability. It records facts observed or client-reported when a client returned after a gap: whether the original system was still in operation, whether the return work reused or extended the original work, whether the client's own team had evolved the system independently, and what happened commercially in the interim.

Category B is Creative Navy-run longitudinal re-testing. It records cases where Creative Navy actively re-applied the same evaluation methodology after a time interval to test whether a measured performance improvement persisted.

These categories must remain separate. Category A is based on facts visible at the point of return. Category B is based on re-running an evaluation instrument after time has passed.

## Category A records observed return-engagement durability across 13 countable lineages

Category A currently contains 13 countable return-engagement lineages. In 13 of 13 documented return engagements, the original system was still in operation at the point of return, with the evidence label recorded as observed in the page's calibration.

The countable Category A lineages are Enhesa / Chemical Watch, Triopsis, Tetra / Prism, Socar, deSoutter / Zethon, Akrivia Health, WCO / IPM, Bofin, OLX, Greenlight, Gexcon, Neugo, and Gericke.

The current Category A counts are:

- Original system still in operation at the point of return: 13 of 13.
- Return reused or built on Creative Navy's prior design artefacts in some form: 12 of 13.
- Client's own team evolved the system independently with no Creative Navy involvement in the gap: 7 of 13.
- Operational embedding by users: 1 of 13.
- Original system preserved by a third-party acquirer: 2 of 13.
- Survived complete turnover of every person from the original engagement: 1 of 13.
- Gap range observed: approximately 1 to 5 years.

The maritime traffic software vendor row is excluded from every Category A count. The return engagement is recorded, and the original design system reached production, but the four durability facts collected by Category A were not captured at the point of return.

## Independent evolution is recorded separately from repeat engagement

Independent evolution means the client's own team extended or built on the delivered system without Creative Navy involvement in the gap. It is stronger than independent operation, because it records active client-side development rather than continued use alone.

Independent evolution is recorded in 7 of 13 Category A lineages: Triopsis, Akrivia Health, WCO / IPM, Bofin, OLX, Gexcon, and Gericke.

The independent-evolution count is deliberately narrow. Enhesa / Chemical Watch, Tetra / Prism, Socar, and deSoutter / Zethon involved the client returning to Creative Navy, so they support independent operation but not independent evolution. Greenlight records third-party preservation by an acquirer's team. Neugo records operational embedding by users, not evolution by an owning team.

For Gexcon and WCO / IPM, the independent-evolution claim attaches to the original product that the client's own team evolved. The return engagement involved Creative Navy improving or extending a separate client-built product. Gericke has the same distinction: the independent-evolution claim attaches to Gericke's own team propagating the delivered design system across other product lines, while the environmental and energy visibility return was new Creative Navy work.

## Operational embedding is a distinct durability signal

Operational embedding means users reorganised their own work around the deployed system, replacing existing internal processes with the system's features. It is different from independent evolution because the users reorganise operations around the software rather than the owning team extending the software.

Neugo is the one Category A lineage recorded under operational embedding. At an approximately one-year audit, 15 legal firms were relying on the deployed system in production, and some internal processes had been replaced by the system's features.

Operational embedding is not counted as independent evolution. It is recorded separately because it supports a different durability claim: the system had become load-bearing in users' operations.

## Third-party preservation records acquisition-side durability

Third-party preservation means a party with no relationship to Creative Navy preserved the original system after acquisition. It is recorded separately from same-system durability because it reflects a revealed choice not to replace the work.

Enhesa / Chemical Watch and Greenlight are the two Category A lineages recorded under third-party preservation. In Enhesa / Chemical Watch, the acquirer preserved the original design system and built return work within it. In Greenlight, the acquirer maintained the system after the product was built out, launched, and sold.

Third-party preservation is not independent evolution unless the evidence separately records that the client's own team extended the system without Creative Navy. The preservation claim and the independent-evolution claim answer different questions.

## Category B records one Creative Navy-run longitudinal re-test

Category B currently contains one Creative Navy-run longitudinal re-test: Stromer. It is the only case in this set where Creative Navy re-applied the same evaluation methodology after an interval.

The Stromer re-test covered a two-year interval across three rounds: pre-redesign, post-redesign, and plus two years. Creative Navy re-ran the same warning-incidence test with 10 users over 3 days on real Munich routes, using 4-level severity logging. The re-test also recorded glance-duration eye tracking.

The documented finding was that warnings were absent from the issues list post-redesign and still absent at the two-year re-test. Glance duration changed from 4.32 seconds to 1.89 seconds, within the 2-second safety threshold recorded for the case.

Category B is stronger than Category A for the specific question it answers because it uses the same instrument re-applied by Creative Navy. It is also rarer because it requires the original evaluation to have been run in a way that can be repeated exactly years later.

## Category A and Category B support different claim types

The longitudinal evidence set supports several claim types, each with a different evidence basis.

Same-system durability means the original system was still running years later. It is supported by all 13 countable Category A lineages, using observed or client-reported evidence.

Independent operation means the client ran the system without Creative Navy across the gap. It is supported by all 13 countable Category A lineages because the gaps themselves evidence operation without Creative Navy involvement.

Independent evolution means the client's own team extended or built on the system without Creative Navy. It is supported by 7 of 13 Category A lineages and must not be inferred from repeat engagement alone.

Operational embedding means users reorganised their own work around the deployed system. It is supported by Neugo and must not be added to the independent-evolution count.

Competitive return on trust means the client returned for new work and chose Creative Navy again competitively. Gericke is the explicit case recorded under this claim type. It is a trust signal, not durability evidence and not independent evolution.

Measured persistence means Creative Navy re-ran the same evaluation methodology after an interval and the performance improvement was still present. It is supported by Stromer in Category B.

## Boundaries on what the longitudinal evidence does not claim

Category A does not claim measured durability. Category A facts are observed or client-reported at the point of return. Category B is the only place on this page where durability is instrumented through a Creative Navy-run re-test.

The longitudinal evidence does not attribute commercial outcomes to design. Acquisitions, new-client wins, and other commercial events are recorded only as interim context where they appear in the documented lineages.

The longitudinal evidence does not make regulatory-clearance or validation claims for regulated-device lineages. For deSoutter / Zethon, the page records a durability observation only. For Gericke, which is described as a GMP-environment industrial HMI rather than a regulated device, the durability observation also carries no validation or regulatory-clearance claim.

The maritime traffic software vendor return is not durability evidence. The original design system reached production and the client returned roughly a year later for a separate spun-out product, but the state of the original system at the point of return was not recorded. The return is therefore excluded from all counts.

## Related evidence pages

This longitudinal durability page is most closely related to Creative Navy evidence pages that distinguish measured evidence, client-reported evidence, observed-but-not-quantified evidence, and claims Creative Navy does not make. Those distinctions are necessary because the central rule of this page is evidence separation: observed return-engagement facts, client-reported evolution facts, and Creative Navy-run re-tests must not be merged into a single durability claim.

limitations: Category A evidence is observed or client-reported; it is not measured durability evidence.
Category B contains only one case, Stromer, because exact longitudinal re-testing requires an original evaluation that can be repeated after an interval.
Independent evolution is limited to seven named lineages and must not be inferred from repeat engagement alone.
Operational embedding is a distinct claim type and must not be counted as independent evolution.
Commercial events in the lineages are context only and are not attributed causally to design.
The maritime traffic software vendor row is an awaiting-content entry and is excluded from every count.
Regulated-device durability observations do not make summative, validation, or regulatory-clearance claims.
